architecture.title: NeMo Relay — the observe → learn → optimize layer under a long-running agent
architecture.caption: A relay wraps every tool and model call of a Hermes turn in a telemetry span, a right-sizing router sends easy prompts to a small model and hard ones to the big one, and one OTel instrumentation fans the same trace out to Phoenix, Datadog or LangSmith — with slow/expensive spans curated as Data Flywheel feedstock. Relay itself is early/limited availability, so you build the substrate: spans, Phoenix, router, OTLP export.

sequence.title: One Hermes turn: spans captured, routed, exported to Phoenix
sequence.caption: The relay measures — it never guesses: token counts come from the API response's usage field, latency from wall-clock timing. The trace then travels to Phoenix over OTLP-HTTP where the span tree becomes inspectable evidence.

steps.label: answer; agent span hermes-turn closes at 2225 ms
HTTP 200 — trace accepted; span tree visible in the UI
curate slow/expensive spans → flywheel JSONL — and remember: 'equal outcome' from routing is a claim until App 09's LLM-judge proves it

charts.title: Where the time goes — span latency in one agent turn
charts.caption: Measured by lab01_build_a_relay.py (TUTORIAL step 2 expected output; your numbers WILL differ — they're measured). The llm span dwarfs the tool spans, which is why the router targets model calls, not tool calls.

charts.title: Right-sizing router — same measured tokens, priced two ways
charts.caption: lab02_rightsize_router.py: the SAME measured tokens priced at illustrative $/M-token tiers — routed is 9% cheaper at (claimed) equal outcome. The saving is dominated by how much easy traffic you have, and the equal-outcome claim needs App 09's LLM-judge before production.
